title: ChronoDuck language-neutral fixture
description: docs/testing/registry-and-fixtures.md's fixture format — enforced in practice by scripts/fixtures-validate.py, which implements these rules directly (dependency-light Python script per Article IV.2) rather than a generic schema interpreter. This file is the canonical field reference.

fixture.description: A slug identifying this fixture, e.g. rate/reset-midwindow/extrapolate/step30

function.description: The registry function name this fixture exercises

samples.description: Each item is [t, v] or [t, v, st]. v is a number, the literal tokens NaN/stale, or a histogram literal object when domain is HISTOGRAM.

expected.description: One entry per grid point; null means no value. Required whenever samples is non-empty — the inert-fixture rule (samples with no expected is not a fixture, it's dead weight).

wrong.description: Optional: named-bug -> value a specific known-wrong implementation returns, for regression naming.

provenance.description: Roster identity and the L12 floor. The kernel stores this and never interprets it — a scan forbids branching on a provenance value. May legitimately contain forbidden-language tokens (e.g. a query-language name) since it is data, not code — scripts/hygiene/forbid-consumer.py scopes its scan to fixture keys, never values, for exactly this reason.

histogramLiteral.description: The grammar a sample's v uses when domain is HISTOGRAM, per docs/testing/registry-and-fixtures.md.

schema.description: Exponential-histogram scale; mutually exclusive with custom_bounds

custom_bounds.description: Classic-histogram bucket boundaries; mutually exclusive with schema
